## AI Review Synthesis

<!-- sepo-agent-review-synthesis -->

> Dual-agent review by **Claude** and **Codex**.
> Requested by @lolipopshock.

## Summary of PR/Issue
PR #414 implements the first bounded `test-lanes` phase from #413, under the broader #409 test redesign. It adds explicit `.agent` scripts for runtime tests, workflow/action checks, docs hygiene checks, shell checks, and a composed `test:ci`. It also updates Test Scripts CI to install, build once, then run visible lane steps, replacing inline Ruby workflow checks with typed Node tests. The larger `envelope.test.ts` breakup and shared harness work are intentionally deferred.

## Review
Overall, reviewers agreed the PR is scoped correctly and safe to merge. One reviewer raised a non-blocking future-hardening concern about lane drift; the other code review and rubrics review found no required issues.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Lane partition drift guard is optional follow-up | WARNING | The `test:runtime` exclusion list can drift from the explicit `check:*` inclusions if future edits update only one side. The partition is complete today and checks pass, so this is a follow-up decision rather than a required PR fix. |

## Progress
- Rubrics review passed with no findings.
- Independent code review found no required issues and verified `test:ci` plus `git diff --check`.
- Current PR checks show `check` passing on head `655382195f420552a34f5599522c2ca6e494c40a`.
- No existing inline comments or review threads were present before synthesis.
- Posted one inline comment on [`.agent/package.json:11`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/414#discussion_r3359350991); no replies, minimizations, or thread resolutions were performed.

## Issue Details
<details>
<summary>Lane partition drift guard is optional follow-up</summary>

**Cause:** `test:runtime` excludes selected compiled tests by name/pattern while the structural lanes re-include them separately. A future edit could add an exclusion without adding the test to another lane.

**Candidate solutions:** Add a small meta-test in the #409 follow-up work that asserts every compiled `dist/**/*.test.js` is claimed by exactly one lane, or keep this as a documented/manual maintenance invariant for now.

**Comments:** This is not a current correctness failure: the current partition is complete, CI is passing, and #413 explicitly keeps larger harness work out of scope.

</details>

## Recommended Next Step
HUMAN_DECISION: The only remaining concern is optional future hardening that maintainers can accept now or defer to #409; it does not require an automated fix-pr pass.
